newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kashmiri, Mexican, Palestinian journalists honored.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri, Mexican, Palestinian journalists honored.

text.p: A Mexican editor exposing corruption, a Kashmiri reporter surviving attempts on his life and a Palestinian journalist who uses the Internet to avoid censorship were awarded prestigious U.S. journalist prizes on Tuesday

In addition, the annual Freedom Awards from the New York-based Committee to Protect Journalists included Ocak Isik Yurtcu, currently in a Turkish jail for 15 years because of his newspaper's reporting on the Kurdish conflict in defiance of government censorship.
The group last year honoured Irish journalist Veronica Guerin, who was assassinated in June, presumably on the orders of drug barons, for her exposure of drug trafficking in her country.

The committee, founded 15 years ago by American journalists, aims to use the power of the U.S. media on behalf of colleagues threatehed abroad. This year's winners appeared at a news conference at the United Nations:
-- J. Jesus Blancornelas, editor in chief of the Zeta weekly Mexican newspaper in Tijuana on the U.S. border, is one of the country's few newspapers continually exposing government corruption.

In 1988, its co-editor, Hector Felix Miranda was murdered by still unidentified assailants who riddled the Zeta offices with gunfire."Among 400 newspapers in Mexico, less than 10 are truly independent," Blancornelas told reporters.
He is credited with bringing about a change in the way many Mexican journalists do buinsess by helping to institute policies that discourage journalists from taking bribes.

-- Yusuf Jameel, a Kashmiri, is a reporter for the Asian Age daily newspaper in Delhi, India, and is cited for fearless reporting of the civil war in Indian-held Kasmir. A former reporter for the British Broadcasting Corporation and a stringer for Reuters, Jameel's reports were considered authoritative by many foreign journalists in the region.

He was injured in 1995 when a letter bomb addressed to him exploded, killing Mushtaq Ali, a cameraman. In 1992 grenades were thrown at his home and office and later that year security officers severly beat him on the head. He has been threatened by militant separatists.

-- Daoud Kuttab, co-director of Internews Middle East and project director of the Arab Media Internet Network has long challenged censorship practices of both the Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority, which he has recently criticised for despotic treatment of the press.

He broke several stories on the Middle East peace process and was the first Palestinian to interview Israeli leaders Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres. But his columns have been rejected by several Arab-language papers, after which he published commentaries in American newspapers. Earlier this year he founded an Internet page to publish articles by Middle East journalists banned elsewhere. He said censorship has been easing because of the Internet and satellite television which made it difficult to control news.

The committee, at its gala annual awards on Tuesday, is also giving Arthur Ochs Sulzburger, former publisher of the New York Times, a lifetime achievement award, mainly for, at the risk of criminal prosecution, publishing the Pentagon papers in 1971 that exposed U.S. involvement in Vietnam.
